correctness.rationale: The graph models are given by exact coordinate adjacency and verified to have the common strongly regular parameters; a complete 2^16-subset exhaustive test agrees coefficient-for-coefficient with a disjoint exhaustive deletion/isolated/pairing recurrence. Both graphs have exact arrays respectively (1,16,120,384,528,144) and (1,16,120,384,544,240,32); the recurrence proof and arithmetic validate every finite claim, while nothing is inferred for larger graphs.

evidence: Primary 2023 paper bounds cubic graphs, so neither graph satisfies its degree hypothesis.
Ordinary independence polynomials for the same pair: 1+16t+72t^2+96t^3+16t^4 versus 1+16t+72t^2+96t^3+24t^4; these count only induced-degree-zero sets.
The current paper counts the larger induced-degree-at-most-one family and obtains 32 six-sets in one graph, 0 in the other.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The present complete dissociation-count statement is not a special case of cubic dissociation bounds or a logical consequence of the previously computed independent-set enumeration/homotopy type, and the classical spectral identity in fact makes the displayed polynomial difference informative.

evidence: Dissociation sets are exactly induced subgraphs consisting of disjoint vertices and edges (equivalently, induced maximum degree at most one).
Same-pair ordinary independence polynomial previously known is not the dissociation polynomial: it counts only configurations with no selected edges.

originality.rationale: The 2023 dissociation-polynomial theorem covers cubic degree-three graphs, whereas both graphs here are degree six; classical cospectrality and recent ordinary independence-complex computations concern different invariants. Multiple exact-value, same-graph, alternate-definition, and spectral-invariant searches did not identify the paired dissociation arrays or number gap. This remains a best-knowledge assessment with unindexed-table risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed published computation or graph database table may already list equivalent coefficients.
The distinction is finite and does not imply a universal theorem for all cospectral or strongly regular graphs.

value.rationale: The only two strongly regular graphs with parameters (16,6,2,2) form a natural canonical test of which invariants are spectral. Complete dissociation arrays agree through degree three for structural reasons but diverge by 16 z^4(1+6 z+2 z^2); their maxima differ by one with exact multiplicities. This is a motivated invariant separation for a natural pair, not an arbitrary parameter slice or claim of a new graph distinction in general.
